feedback: Written before this candidate has raced, so no outcome is claimed. Evidence: iteration 3 (y=0.07 m, +/-0.05 m, radius 0.03 m, 51.31) gave the best s-bend progress (0.155), with one line-loss event per run on s-bend and slalom and slalom max_error 0.065 m. Iteration 7 (y=0.065 m, +/-0.065 m) scored 35.77, with slalom line loss again and s-bend progress back to 0.04. Iteration 6 (radius 0.04 m) brought line loss back and cut s-bend progress to 0.1325, so ground speed should stay at 0.03 m. Slalom steering_oscillation stayed at 0.13 to 0.14 at rows y=0.05, 0.06, 0.065 and 0.07 m, so the lead does not drive it. The oval has been stuck at progress 0.115 and max_error about 0.061 m since iteration 1, so geometry may not fix it. What I had to compensate for: I kept kp 2.0, kd 0.10 and ki 0, because the narrower 0.09 m track already raises turn gain. The weights [-2,-1,0,1,2] keep the signal within about +/-2 across the wider spread. Next race: if line loss is zero on s-bend and slalom and slalom max_error is below 0.06 m, keep the +/-0.065 m spread at y=0.07 m. If line loss returns at y=0.07 m with the wider spread, the lead is the trigger at this speed. Then keep the spread and try y=0.067 m, not a bigger lead. If slalom max_error stays at or above 0.06 m with zero line loss, widen the spread to +/-0.08 m with 16 mm footprints.
requested_changes: If line_loss_events return at sensor y=0.07 m with the +/-0.065 m spread (iteration 3 had one per run at +/-0.05 m, iteration 7 one per run at y=0.065 m), keep the spread and set y=0.067 m to test whether a slightly smaller lead cuts the loss while keeping most of the s-bend gain.

If line loss is zero and slalom max_error is still at or above 0.06 m (iteration 3 gave 0.065 m, iteration 7 gave 0.0642 m), widen sensor x to +/-0.08 m with 16 mm footprints, since the 0.065 m spread may still let the line leave view on slalom bends.

If the score is at or above 51.3 with zero line loss, keep geometry fixed and test sensor_size 0.012 m at the same positions, to check whether a smaller footprint reduces the jitter that the 16 mm footprint may add.
